name: Incline bodyweight trainer
aliases: Total Gym-style trainer; Glide board gym; Incline sled trainer
description: A sliding seat on an adjustable incline rail with cables: you pull or push yourself up the slope, so steeper angles mean more load. Folds flat for storage.

adjustability: Incline adjusts in 6–12 levels; some take add-on weight bars.
signature_exercises: Incline pull-up; Incline row; Squat; Chest press; Pullover
buying_tips: Check the user weight limit and how flat it folds.

signature_exercises: Rope pushdown; Cable curl; Face pull; Single-arm lat pulldown; Straight-arm pulldown

description: A seated station that braces you for supported hamstring, back, chest and hip stretches; leg stretchers spread the legs for splits.
signature_exercises: Seated hamstring stretch; Hip opener; Chest stretch
buying_tips: Leg stretchers are cheap for splits; full stations are commercial.
safety: Use controlled pressure.

name: Bulgarian bag
aliases: Crescent sandbag; Suples bag
description: A crescent-shaped weighted bag with handles, swung and spun around the body for rotational strength.
signature_exercises: Bulgarian bag spin; Bag snatch; Arm throw; Bag squat
buying_tips: Start light (5–10 kg) because the spin loads the shoulders.
safety: Keep a clear radius around you when spinning.

name: Indian clubs
aliases: Steel clubs; Clubbells; Persian meels
description: Bottle-shaped clubs swung in patterns to build shoulder mobility, grip and rotational strength.
adjustability: Fixed per club; usually bought as a pair.
signature_exercises: Club arm cast; Club mill; Club shield cast; Club swipe
buying_tips: Light wooden clubs suit mobility; steel clubbells suit strength.
safety: Start light and swing in a clear area.

name: Sledgehammer
aliases: Sledge; Training hammer; Shock hammer
description: A heavy hammer swung onto a tyre or mat for rotational power and conditioning.
weight_options: 4–10 kg (8–20 lb); training hammers have rubber heads
adjustability: Fixed; use a lighter or heavier hammer to scale.
signature_exercises: Sledgehammer tyre strikes; Alternating overhead strikes; Sledgehammer levering; Side-to-side chops
buying_tips: A shock-absorbing hammer is kinder on your elbows than a builder's sledge.
safety: Keep a clear radius around you and strike a tyre that won't bounce it back.

name: Farmer's walk handles
aliases: Farmer's handles; Farmers carry handles; Farmer walk implements
description: A pair of loadable handles with a central grip used to carry heavy weights in each hand.
adjustability: Plate-loaded; some have thicker or rotating handles.
signature_exercises: Farmer's carry; Suitcase carry; Farmer's hold for time; Farmer's walk turn
buying_tips: Check handle height (pick height) and diameter; pairs are often sold together.
safety: Set them down under control at the end, not by dropping them on toes.

name: Pulling harness
aliases: Truck pull harness; Sled harness; Prowler harness
description: A padded harness worn over the shoulders or waist to drag sleds, tyres or vehicles.
signature_exercises: Forward sled drag; Truck pull; Tyre drag; Backward sled drag
buying_tips: Look for wide padded straps and a strong D-ring.
safety: Check the rope and clips before a heavy pull.

name: Arm-over-arm rope pull
aliases: Truck pull machine; Rope pull sled; Hand-over-hand pull
description: A station or sled you pull towards you hand over hand with a thick rope while seated or braced.
adjustability: Machines have adjustable resistance; a sled is adjusted with plates.
signature_exercises: Arm-over-arm sled pull; Seated rope pull; Truck pull (arm over arm)
buying_tips: A thick rope and a sled with an anchor point is the cheap home version.
safety: Wear gloves or tape to avoid rope burns.
keywords: rope pull truck arm over arm

name: Atlas stone
aliases: Stone; Concrete stone; Natural stone
description: A round concrete ball lifted from the floor and loaded onto a platform or over a bar.
weight_options: 40–200+ kg (90–440 lb); home moulds to cast your own
adjustability: Fixed weight; buy a set or cast several sizes from a mould.
signature_exercises: Atlas stone load; Stone over bar; Stone lap and shoulder; Stone carry
buying_tips: A mould lets you cast stones cheaply; use tacky and arm sleeves to protect forearms.
safety: Lap the stone before extending and keep feet clear when dropping it.

name: Axle bar
aliases: Fat bar; Thick bar; Apollon axle
description: A thick (about 5 cm) bar with no rotating sleeves or knurl, used in strongman. Builds grip and makes deadlifts and cleans much harder to hold.
signature_exercises: Axle deadlift; Axle clean and press; Axle row; Axle curl
buying_tips: Use with a belt-clean style; check the bar holds Olympic plates without slipping.
keywords: axle fat bar thick bar strongman apollon

name: Car deadlift frame
aliases: Deadlift frame; Car deadlift
description: A lever frame lifted from long handles, mimicking lifting the back of a car.
weight_options: Lever plus plates; up to 400+ kg
signature_exercises: Car deadlift; Frame deadlift for reps
buying_tips: A trap bar with high handles is the practical home stand-in.
safety: Brace hard and keep the lower back neutral.

name: Circus dumbbell
aliases: Thick-handled dumbbell; Strongman dumbbell
description: An oversized single dumbbell with a thick, often rotating handle, cleaned and pressed overhead one-handed.
signature_exercises: Circus dumbbell clean and press; One-arm push press; Circus dumbbell hold
buying_tips: A rotating handle is closer to competition spec.
safety: Use the free hand to help clean it and keep the wrist stacked.

name: Conan's wheel
aliases: Conan's wheel of pain; Strongman wheel
description: A long weighted arm anchored to a central pivot; you hold the end in a Zercher position and walk it around in a circle.
adjustability: Plate-loaded arm; fixed pivot bolted to the floor.
signature_exercises: Conan's wheel carry; Zercher hold walk
buying_tips: Needs a lot of floor space and anchoring; mostly a gym or competition piece.
safety: Clear the circle before you start walking.

name: Fingal's fingers
aliases: Fingal fingers; Pole flip
description: A row of hinged poles of increasing weight that you lift from horizontal and push over to the other side.
adjustability: Fixed per pole; some home versions are plate-loaded.
signature_exercises: Fingal's fingers flip; Pole walk-up
buying_tips: Rarely sold for home use; look for strongman gyms with one.
safety: Walk the pole up in a straight line and step clear when it falls.

name: Frame carry
aliases: Farmer's frame; Carry frame
description: A rectangular steel frame you stand inside and carry by two long side handles, loaded with plates.
adjustability: Fixed; plates on loading posts at each end.
signature_exercises: Frame carry; Frame pick and hold; Frame deadlift
buying_tips: Usually a competition piece; check the handle length fits your stride.
safety: Keep the frame level and step with short, quick steps.

name: Husafell stone
aliases: Odd-object stone; Carry stone; Natural stone
description: A flat, awkward stone or steel replica hugged against the chest and carried for distance.
adjustability: Fixed; steel versions can be plate-loaded.
signature_exercises: Husafell stone carry; Bear-hug carry; Stone hold for time
buying_tips: Plate-loaded steel versions are easier to store and adjust.
safety: Lift it close to the body to protect the lower back.

name: Keg
aliases: Beer keg; Strongman keg
description: A steel beer keg filled with water or sand and lifted, carried, loaded or tossed.
adjustability: Change the weight by adding or removing water or sand.
signature_exercises: Keg carry; Keg load; Keg toss; Keg clean and press
buying_tips: Use an empty keg (not a deposit keg you must return); water sloshes, sand does not.
safety: Check the caps are tight so it doesn't leak or burst.

name: Power stairs
aliases: Duck walk implement; Stair implement
description: A handled weight lifted up a set of steps one step at a time.
weight_options: Implement 30–60 kg plus plates; steps ~40 cm
signature_exercises: Power stairs; Duck walk; Implement deadlift
buying_tips: Usually a gym piece; a farmer handle and sturdy box can mimic it.
safety: Keep the implement swinging between the legs, not into the step.

name: Stone platform
aliases: Atlas stone loader; Stone loading platform; Stone ramp
description: A sturdy platform or set of stepped platforms of fixed heights onto which atlas stones are loaded.
adjustability: Some have adjustable heights or a stone ramp to return stones.
signature_exercises: Atlas stone load; Stone series; Sandbag load to platform
buying_tips: Pick one with a lip to stop stones rolling off and a height you can adjust.
safety: Make sure it can't tip when a heavy stone hits the edge.

name: Strongman log
aliases: Log bar; Log press bar
description: A thick cylindrical bar with neutral handles cut inside it, cleaned to the chest and pressed overhead.
adjustability: Fixed diameter; choose 10 in or 12 in. Handles fixed.
signature_exercises: Log clean and press; Log push press; Log clean; Log strict press
buying_tips: Start with a 10 in log; check handle spacing and knurling. Fillable steel logs are cheaper.
safety: Clean it with a belly roll and keep the elbows up so it doesn't crush the sternum.

name: Strongman shield
aliases: Shield carry; Strongman plate shield
description: A large, flat steel shield hugged against the chest and carried for distance.
signature_exercises: Shield carry; Bear-hug hold
buying_tips: Plate-loaded shields let you scale the load.
safety: Keep it high on the chest so it doesn't hit your knees.

name: Strongman tacky
aliases: Tacky; Stone tack; Pine tar grip
description: A sticky grip paste used on forearms and hands to hold atlas stones and other odd objects.
signature_exercises: Atlas stone load; Stone over bar; Keg load
buying_tips: Many gyms ban it; buy one with a remover and check your gym's rules.

name: Tyre
aliases: Tire; Flip tyre; Tractor tyre
description: A large truck or tractor tyre flipped end over end, or hit with a sledgehammer, for full-body power and conditioning.
adjustability: Fixed; add chains or plates inside to make it heavier.
signature_exercises: Tyre flip; Tyre sledgehammer strikes; Tyre jumps; Tyre drag
buying_tips: Farm and tyre shops often give used tyres away; choose one you can flip for at least a few reps.
safety: Drive with hips and legs, not a rounded back, and never curl it up with straight arms.

name: Viking press
aliases: Viking press station; Landmine viking press
description: A lever-arm pressing station with two handles at the end, pressed overhead from shoulder height.
adjustability: Many have adjustable handle height or swap-in handles.
signature_exercises: Viking press; Viking push press; Landmine viking press
buying_tips: A landmine with a viking handle attachment is the space-saving option.
safety: Lock your trunk so you don't over-arch the lower back.

name: Yoke
aliases: Strongman yoke; Super yoke; Yoke bar
description: A tall steel frame with a crossbar that sits across your upper back; you load it with plates and walk with it.
adjustability: Fixed frame; many have adjustable crossbar height. Some double as a squat stand.
signature_exercises: Yoke carry; Yoke walk for distance; Yoke pick and hold; Yoke squat
buying_tips: Check crossbar height adjustment and whether it converts to a rack; wide feet reduce wobble.
safety: Practise drops and keep the run path clear before loading heavy.

name: Boxing gloves
aliases: Bag gloves; Sparring gloves; Training gloves; Muay Thai gloves
description: Padded gloves that protect your hands (and partners) on bags, pads and in sparring.
signature_exercises: Heavy bag rounds; Pad work; Sparring
buying_tips: 14–16 oz for general training and sparring; hook-and-loop is easiest solo.
safety: Always wrap hands underneath.

name: Double-end bag
aliases: Floor-to-ceiling ball; Double end ball
description: A small ball fixed by elastic cords to floor and ceiling that springs back for accuracy and slipping drills.
signature_exercises: Double-end bag rounds; Jab and slip; Counter punching
buying_tips: Need solid floor and ceiling anchors; tension changes the speed.
safety: Wear light gloves to protect knuckles.

name: Focus mitts
aliases: Pads; Punch mitts; Hook and jab pads
description: Hand-held padded targets a partner wears so you can drill punch combinations and defence.
signature_exercises: Pad combinations; Jab-cross on mitts; Slip and counter
buying_tips: Curved mitts with good wrist support help the holder.
safety: The holder should meet, not push into, the punch.

name: Freestanding punching bag
aliases: Free-standing bag; Pedestal bag; Water-base bag
description: A punching bag on a base filled with water or sand, so it needs no ceiling mount.
weight_options: Base 100–150 kg when filled; 150–180 cm tall
signature_exercises: Bag rounds; Jab-cross; Roundhouse kicks; Front kicks; Knees
buying_tips: Fill the base with sand for less sliding; uppercuts are limited on most models.
safety: Put it on a mat so it doesn't creep across the floor.

name: Groin guard
aliases: Cup; Groin protector; Jockstrap cup
description: A protective cup or guard worn for kicking sports and sparring.
signature_exercises: Kickboxing sparring; Muay Thai clinch
buying_tips: Steel cups are standard for Muay Thai.

name: Hand wraps
aliases: Boxing wraps; Gel wraps; Quick wraps
description: Cloth strips wound around the hands and wrists under gloves to support knuckles and wrists.
signature_exercises: Heavy bag rounds; Pad work; Speed bag

safety: Wrap firmly across the knuckles but not tight enough to numb fingers.

name: Headgear
aliases: Head guard; Sparring helmet
description: Padded headgear worn for sparring to reduce cuts and bruising.
signature_exercises: Sparring; Partner drills
buying_tips: Check it doesn't block your vision when you tuck your chin.
safety: It reduces cuts, not concussion risk; spar sensibly.

name: Kick shield
aliases: Strike shield; Kick bag shield
description: A large, thick hand-held pad for full-power kicks, knees and pushes.
signature_exercises: Push kicks; Side kicks; Power kicks
buying_tips: Curved shields absorb more of the kick for the holder.

name: Martial arts mats
aliases: Tatami; Judo mats; Grappling mats; Jigsaw mats
description: Thick foam mats that cushion falls for grappling, throws and floor work.
signature_exercises: Breakfalls; Grappling drills; Throws; Ground work
buying_tips: 4 cm is the minimum for throws; jigsaw mats are fine for drilling.

name: MMA gloves
aliases: Grappling gloves; Hybrid gloves; Open-finger gloves
description: Thin open-finger gloves that allow grappling as well as striking.
signature_exercises: Ground and pound; MMA bag work; Grappling
buying_tips: 7 oz hybrid gloves are better for sparring than 4 oz fight gloves.
safety: They give less protection; go lighter on heavy bags.

name: Mouthguard
aliases: Gum shield; Mouth guard
description: A shaped guard over the teeth to protect them and the jaw during sparring and contact.
signature_exercises: Sparring; Grappling; Contact drills
buying_tips: Boil-and-bite is fine to start; custom-fit is worth it for regular sparring.
safety: Wear one for any contact sparring.

name: Reflex bag
aliases: Reflex ball stand; Spinning reflex bar; Boxing reflex ball
description: A ball or pad on a spring-loaded stand (or headband) that rebounds quickly for speed and reaction drills.
signature_exercises: Reflex ball punches; Jab and slip; Rapid combinations
buying_tips: A weighted base that doesn't tip matters more than the ball.

name: Shin guards
aliases: Shin pads; Shin and instep guards
description: Padded guards covering the shin and instep for kicking pads, bags and sparring partners.
signature_exercises: Roundhouse kicks; Checking kicks; Kickboxing sparring
buying_tips: Strapped guards with instep protection stay put better.

name: Slip bag
aliases: Maize bag; Slip ball
description: A small weighted ball hung on a rope at head height for practising slipping and head movement.
signature_exercises: Slip drills; Bob and weave; Counter jab
buying_tips: A tennis ball in a sock on a string is a free stand-in.

name: Thai pads
aliases: Kick pads; Muay Thai pads; Thai kick pads
description: Long forearm-strapped pads a partner holds for kicks, knees, elbows and punches.
signature_exercises: Roundhouse kicks on pads; Teep; Knee strikes; Elbows
buying_tips: Curved pads with double straps hold up to kicks.

name: Wall bag
aliases: Wall pad; Wall-mounted punching pad
description: A padded target screwed to the wall for punching where there is no room for a hanging bag.
signature_exercises: Jab-cross; Hooks; Punch-outs
buying_tips: Mount to studs or masonry, not plasterboard.
safety: Wrap and glove up; the wall gives no swing.

name: Grappling dummy
aliases: Throwing dummy; BJJ dummy; Wrestling dummy
description: A weighted human-shaped bag with limbs for practising throws, takedowns, ground and pound and submissions.
signature_exercises: Dummy throws; Ground and pound; Guard passing; Mount transitions
buying_tips: A dummy with legs that can be posed suits BJJ; a heavier one suits throws.
safety: Throw onto mats only.

name: Speed bag
aliases: Speed ball; Speed bag platform; Rebound platform
description: A small air-filled bag hung from a rebound platform and hit rhythmically for hand speed, timing and shoulder endurance.
signature_exercises: Speed bag rounds; Fist rolling; Triplets; Alternating punches
buying_tips: Buy the platform and bag together; a heavy, stiff platform gives a cleaner rebound.
safety: Set the bag at mouth height so you don't strain the shoulders.

name: Torso dummy
aliases: BOB dummy; Body opponent bag; Mannequin bag
description: A freestanding human-shaped target for accurate strikes to head and body.
signature_exercises: Target combinations; Head-body combinations; Elbows
buying_tips: Fill with sand rather than water for stability.

name: Belly pad
aliases: Body protector; Trainer belly pad
description: A thick body protector a coach wears so you can land body shots and teeps.
signature_exercises: Teeps to the body; Body hooks; Knee strikes
buying_tips: Mainly for coaches; check strap adjustment.

name: Boxing ring
aliases: Ring; MMA cage; Octagon
description: A raised, roped (or caged) square for sparring and bouts.
signature_exercises: Sparring; Ring cutting drills
buying_tips: A gym fixture; floor rings are cheaper than raised ones.

name: Uppercut bag
aliases: Angle bag; Wall uppercut bag; Teardrop bag
description: A bag shaped or mounted so you can throw uppercuts and hooks at an angle, which a straight heavy bag can't take well.
signature_exercises: Uppercuts; Body hooks; Shovel hooks
buying_tips: Wall-mounted versions save space.
safety: Wrap hands; uppercuts stress the wrists.

name: Agility ladder

description: Small plastic speed hurdles (15–30 cm) or adjustable hurdles for hops, bounds and stepping drills.

buying_tips: Collapsible plastic hurdles are safest because they bend if you clip them.

description: A small rubber ball with knobbly sides that bounces unpredictably, for reaction time and hand-eye coordination.

name: Sandbell

description: A floppy, sand-filled disc bag with no handles that you slam, throw, carry and twist with.
signature_exercises: Sandbell slam; Rotational slam; Russian twist; Sandbell press

name: Slam ball
aliases: Dead ball; No-bounce ball; D-ball
description: A heavy, dead-bounce ball with a thick shell, sand-filled so it doesn't bounce back when you slam it to the floor.
signature_exercises: Medicine ball slam; Rotational slam; Overhead backward throw; Ball-over-shoulder
buying_tips: Textured shells are easier to grip with sweaty hands; heavy ones double as strongman-style shouldering balls.
safety: Slam on rubber flooring, not concrete or wood.

name: Slide board
aliases: Lateral slide board; Slideboard; Skate board trainer
description: A long slick board with stop bumpers at each end; you slide side to side in booties, like speed skating.

safety: Wear the booties and keep shoes off the board.

name: Speed parachute
aliases: Sprint parachute; Resistance parachute; Speed chute
description: A small parachute clipped to a waist belt that catches air as you sprint, adding resistance that grows with speed.
signature_exercises: Parachute sprint; Release sprints; Resisted acceleration runs

name: Speed rope

signature_exercises: Double unders; Triple unders; Speed skipping; Single-leg jump rope
